clue.text: Wealthy puritan concealing repulsive ends, oddly

indicators.note: concealing means one word is hidden inside the other

parts.note: a prig is a smug, morally strict person
vile means repulsive

indicators.note: oddly means take the first and third letters of the word ends

explanation.surface: A rich puritan hides his repellent purposes, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' signals a container; 'oddly' takes the first and third letters of 'ends'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being privileged means enjoying the advantages of money and rank, so it serves as a synonym for wealthy.

clue.text: Rod's sweetheart cut up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E
to lop is to cut

explanation.surface: Rod's girlfriend is very upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is the middle of 'sweet', E; 'up' reverses ELOP. 'cut up' looks like distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole is a long rod or staff, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Smart guy holding old man powerless

parts.note: in means fashionable or smart

indicators.note: holding means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a guy is a rope or cable used to steady a tent or mast
pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A clever bloke supporting his helpless father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart guy' reads as one figure but splits; a guy is a tent rope. 'holding' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incapable cannot act, which makes them powerless or helpless.

clue.text: I broadcast on the radio

parts.note: radio operators spell each letter out with a code word from the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of being a radio presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet used on radio, the letter I is spoken as a country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio code word for the letter I is the name of the South Asian country.

clue.text: English team embarrassed about flop finally departed

indicators.note: about means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football side

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word flop

parts.note: red means blushing, embarrassed

explanation.surface: The England side, red-faced after a failure, finally left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts P, from 'flop' via 'finally', inside XI, an eleven-player team.
explanation.definitionFit: Expired means died, which is the euphemistic sense of departed.

clue.text: He or I could be one

definitions.text: He or I could be one

parts.words: He or I could be one
parts.note: He and I look like pronouns but are chemical symbols for helium and iodine

explanation.surface: A person saying either he or I might be the one.
explanation.walkthrough: He and I look like pronouns but are the chemical symbols for helium and iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium and iodine are both substances in the periodic table.

clue.text: Virtually junk food?

definitions.meaning: unwanted junk email, rubbish arriving in the virtual world of the internet
the tinned luncheon meat sold under that brand name

explanation.surface: Is this processed stuff barely more than junk food?
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both electronic junk mail and a cheap canned pork product.

clue.text: Empty pot catching fresh seafood

indicators.note: catching means one piece holds the other inside
Empty means the inside of the word is removed, leaving its ends

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot
raw means fresh, uncooked

explanation.surface: An empty pot trapping fresh shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' removes the middle of the pot's synonym, a trimmed word; 'catching' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn is a small shellfish eaten as seafood, an example of the category.

clue.text: Stock's recipe contained in quality soup

parts.note: a mine is a rich stock or supply, as in a mine of information; with the 's it gives MINES

indicators.note: contained in means one letter goes inside the word

parts.note: tone means quality, as of sound
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A stock recipe used in a fine soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' and 'soup' look like the kitchen pairing; stock is MINE. 'contained in' puts R inside TONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is the thick Italian vegetable soup.

clue.text: Sensible being held back by ridicule

indicators.note: back says those enclosed letters are read in reverse
being held means the letters sit inside the word ridicule

explanation.surface: A rational person kept back by mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being held' finds DICUL inside 'ridicule'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucid person thinks clearly, so the word is a synonym for sensible or rational.

clue.text: Fate of single Communist leader ousted in torment

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pain means torment

indicators.note: ousted means the named letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: a single is a record released on its own

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Communist

explanation.surface: The destiny of a lone Communist chief expelled amid suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fate' is a verb here. 'leader' takes C, 'ousted' drops it, 'in' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To fate something is to decree its outcome in advance, which is what to preordain means.

clue.text: Polishes some lederhosen if erroneously held up

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means those letters read from bottom to top
some means part of the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Shines leather shorts wrongly hung up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' finds SENIFER across 'lederhosen if erroneously'; 'held up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To refine is to improve by removing flaws, which is the figurative sense of polishing.

clue.text: Middle of Cyprus with say, open plain

indicators.note: Middle of means the central letters of the word Cyprus
say means the word is spoken, so it gives a sound-alike

parts.note: airy means open and spacious

explanation.surface: The heart of Cyprus, with an open plain, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals a sound-alike: AIRY, meaning open, is heard as the ending AIRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a vast flat grassland, a plain especially of North America.

clue.text: Grind first in set, putting in new teeth

indicators.note: putting in means one letter is placed inside the word

parts.note: fag is British slang for tedious hard work, a grind

indicators.note: first in means the opening letter of the word set

explanation.surface: Grind first in a set before fitting new dentures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting in' puts N inside FAG; 'first in' takes S from 'set'. FAG is British slang for drudgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Fangs are long pointed teeth, as in a dog or snake.

clue.text: Fuel runs German car in works

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a plant is a factory or works
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
Opel is a German car maker

explanation.surface: Fuel powers a German car in the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' is a factory, not 'operates'; 'in' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A propellant is a fuel burned to drive a rocket or engine.

clue.text: Reverberation of gong echoed inside head then died

indicators.note: inside means one piece is placed within another

parts.note: to run something is to head it

indicators.note: echoed suggests the sound coming back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a gong is slang for a medal or honour such as the OBE

explanation.surface: The ring of a gong sounded inside someone's head, then faded.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'gong' is British slang for a medal or honour, here the Order of the British Empire. 'echoed' reverses it; 'inside' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebound is a bouncing back, as a sound reverberates off a surface.

clue.text: A French monsieur purchasing exclusive cream

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: purchasing means getting hold of, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: monsieur means gentleman, gent
U means upper class, exclusive

explanation.surface: A Frenchman buying a pricey cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchasing' puts U inside GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An unguent is a soothing ointment or cream.

clue.text: Foreign port providing extra tart

definitions.meaning: a Moroccan seaport on the Strait of Gibraltar

explanation.surface: A port abroad that supplies an extra sharp pie.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan city's name is also the comparative of tangy, meaning sharper-tasting.

clue.text: Great aroma nicely coming over covers lover

indicators.note: coming over says the hidden letters are read backwards
covers means these words hold the letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lovely scent wafts across and envelops a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'covers lover' as the definition; 'covers' is the hidden indicator and 'lover' alone defines. 'coming over' reverses ATAROMANI.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman with whom one is in love, a female lover.

clue.text: Heartless proposal limits vows

indicators.note: Heartless means the middle of the word proposal is removed, leaving its ends

parts.note: edges are limits or borders

explanation.surface: A proposal of marriage without love limits one's promises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' strips proposal to PL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pledges are solemn promises, the same thing as vows.

clue.text: Support for spur round horse's middle

indicators.note: round means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to stir up is to spur or provoke

indicators.note: middle means the central letter of the word horse

explanation.surface: A rider's support device, with a spur, goes round the horse's belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spur' looks like riding kit but means STIR UP; 'round' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup is the loop that supports a rider's foot.

clue.text: Jack in sailor's vessel going around area

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; with the 's it gives ABS

indicators.note: going around means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a tin is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: A Jack aboard a sailor's boat circling a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a sailor (Jack tar), but 'Jack in' is the definition. 'going around' puts A inside TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack in is British slang for giving something up, as one refrains from or forgoes it.

clue.text: Hopes a good endless sleep includes dreams' ending

indicators.note: includes means one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: pi is short for pious, good

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: rest means sleep

indicators.note: ending means the last letter of the word dreams'

explanation.surface: Wishes for a good, unending sleep full of dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of the sleep word; 'includes' puts the final letter of 'dreams'' inside; 'ending' picks it.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to aim for or long for, the same sense as to hope.

clue.text: Yale's leading European philosopher

parts.note: Yale is a brand of door lock

indicators.note: leading means the first letter of the word European

explanation.surface: A top European thinker at Yale University.
explanation.walkthrough: Yale looks like the university but is the lock maker.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was the seventeenth-century English empiricist thinker.

clue.text: Rapid fire reported

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so the word is a sound-alike

parts.note: to shoot is to fire

explanation.surface: A rapid volley of gunfire heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rapid' is a noun here, a stretch of fast water.
explanation.definitionFit: A chute is a steep fall or channel of fast-flowing water, a rapid.

clue.text: Sort of painting I think is about done

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: IMO is text shorthand for in my opinion
past means over and done

explanation.surface: I reckon the type of picture is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I think' is the texting shorthand for in my opinion; 'about' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is a technique of laying paint on thickly so brush strokes stand proud.

clue.text: Volley from cricket ground's lofted, left to fall

indicators.note: to fall means the letter drops lower down the word
lofted means sent upward, so in a down clue the letters read in reverse

parts.note: the Oval is a London cricket ground; with the 's it gives OVALS

explanation.surface: A shot hit high from the cricket ground, left to drop.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground. 'lofted' reverses OVALS to SLAVO; 'to fall' drops L down a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a volley.

clue.text: Haggard woman embracing old loafer

indicators.note: embracing means one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: She is H. Rider Haggard's novel about the immortal queen Ayesha

explanation.surface: A careworn woman hugging her lazy old man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like gaunt but is the novelist Rider Haggard; 'loafer' is not an idler but footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer is a slip-on casual leather shoe, an example of footwear.

clue.text: Playboy's admired until the rapture ends, right?

indicators.note: ends means the first and last letters of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A womaniser is adored until the passion fades, isn't that so?
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes both ends of each word: AD, UL, TE, RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A playboy who sleeps around while married is unfaithful, which is a fair cryptic stretch for a cheating spouse.

clue.text: Control cat perhaps, grabbing one's tail

indicators.note: grabbing means one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip, used to lash

indicators.note: tail means the last letter of the word one

explanation.surface: Keep the cat in check by seizing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' is the whip, cat o' nine tails; 'grabbing' puts E inside LASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead or restraint is a means of control, and to keep on a tight leash is to control.

clue.text: Precious little time to start

indicators.note: to start means the time letter is placed at the front

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small or little

explanation.surface: Hardly any time to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious little' looks like a phrase but splits: 'Precious' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means affectedly dainty or quaint, the overrefined sense of precious.

clue.text: See almost heroic astronaut's outside in orbit

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: epic means heroic in scale

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: scope means range or sphere, an orbit of influence

indicators.note: outside means the outer letters of the word astronaut

explanation.surface: Watch the nearly heroic spacefarer's spacewalk in orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a bishop's diocese, not looking. 'almost' cuts EPIC to EPI; 'outside' gives AT, put 'in' SCOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's jurisdiction, and the episcopate is a bishop's office or term of rule.
